segments.en: Sections 25 through 35 · Continuing the Alef-Bais

segments.he: שְׁאָר שַׁבָּת ש ת א ב ר ש
segments.en: The second letters of the word שְׁאָר [she'or — leaven/remnant] are the letters שַׁבָּת [Shabbos] — for after ש [shin] comes ת [tav], and after א [alef] comes ב [bais], and after ר [reish] comes ש [shin] — which are the letters of Shabbos in reverse [l'mafreia]. For the essential nullification of chametz [leaven] and she'or [sourdough] in the dough — which is the yetzer hara that obstructs [one] from doing His blessed will, and is the aspect of the other god [ail acher], forced apostasy [shmad], G-d forbid — the essential nullification is through the holiness of Shabbos. For then the metzach haratzon [the forehead of will] is revealed — the aspect of ra'ava d'ra'avin [the will of all wills]. And from there the Tzadik draws the supreme encompassing redemption [pidyon elyon hakolel] — until he nullifies the she'or aforementioned and elevates [one] from shmad to ratzon [will].

The essential blemish of faith in the sages comes from those who dispute the truly wise sages — because they are wise in their own eyes in the futile wisdoms of this world, all of which are wisdoms of falsehood — since through these wisdoms one does not merit the true and eternal purpose. And in truth the root of all these wisdoms — whether the outright external wisdoms of the philosophical investigators, or the ordinary wisdoms of the world that are against the point of truth — all derive solely from the fact that their entire intention is only for the sake of the bodily desires. Which is the aspect of weekday eating [achilas chol], where the liver is nourished first and afterwards the brain. And through the holiness of the delight of Shabbos [oneg Shabbos] — when the brain is nourished first — through this — [through this] — all the aforementioned disputants are subdued, and the faith in the sages is repaired.

The greatness of the commandment of the Kiddush Levanah [sanctification of the new moon] is very precious — as our Sages of blessed memory said. And it alludes to the renewal of the world in the time to come — for Israel is destined to be renewed like it. And since the essential faith in the renewal of the world is drawn through the prayer of the [Tzadik who is the] ba'al ko'ach [master of power] — through which the clouds, which are the sitra achra, dissolve and are gone in the aspect of: "I have wiped away your transgressions like a cloud, etc." [Isaiah 44:22] — as explained in the inner teachings — therefore the moon may only be sanctified when the clouds are not covering it.

But regarding those who are meticulous not to sanctify it even when it is visible through a thin and light cloud — all of this is out of great love for the commandment, wishing it to be completely clear and pure. But they did not intend well in this. For in this low and dark world — especially now, in these generations, when the sitra achra has spread very greatly — if we wish to be so meticulous in all the commandments and wait until we can fulfill them with great clarity and purity and brightness, especially with the purity of thought which is the essential — then all the Torah and commandments would already be nullified, G-d forbid. And in truth we must fulfill all the commandments as best we can. And only through this do we keep ourselves alive in this bitter exile — in the very slightest light that shines upon us from within the depth of this very darkness and gloom. And if we wish to be scrupulous and stringent with excessive stringencies — we could stumble and fall through this even more, G-d forbid. Therefore certainly, far be it from us to withhold from the commandment of Kiddush Levanah on account of the aforementioned scrupulosities. Rather, we must fulfill it as our Sages of blessed memory said in the Gemara and the Poskim — that one is obligated to sanctify it even when it is visible through a thin cloud. Especially when the time is pressed and close to the end of the time for sanctification. Especially in winter.

The twelve lunar months correspond to the twelve versions of the prayer [nuscha'os hatefilah] — corresponding to the twelve tribes. And the leap month is corresponding to the tribe of Yosef — who was divided into two tribes. And the essential purpose of the leap [ibur] is to align the solar years with the lunar years — that is, to join the twelve tribes, which are the aspect of the twelve versions of the prayer, to the aspect of Yaakov — who is the aspect of the very substance of truth, the aspect of the sun [chamah]. And through this comes the essential perfection of the prayer.

Through being careful about chametz for seven days and eating matzah — through this the da'as [knowledge/awareness] of faith in Providence is revealed. Until one knows in truth that even nature itself — which is the aspect of chametz — also conducts itself solely through His blessed Providence. For G-d created everything and governs everything through His will. And therefore afterwards eating chametz is also permitted.

A person must remember very — [very] — well all the days of his life, each and every day, the day he departed from the land of Egypt — as it is written: "So that you will remember the day of your departure from the land of Egypt, etc." [Deuteronomy 16:3]. That is: how he departed from Egypt before the appointed time, only through His kindness — and because of this, what passes over him now passes over him. For in every generation a person is obligated to see himself as if he personally left Egypt. For all of the above passes over every person. And therefore one must remember each and every day the greatness of His blessed kindness — that He brought him out from where He brought him out, which is the aspect of the exodus from Egypt. And even though now what passes over him passes over him — even so, certainly the kindness and goodness that G-d has done with him is certainly not in vain, G-d forbid. Rather, he must now pass through these matters and be tested through them. But in the end G-d will complete His part — and he will merit to draw close to His blessed service and to find all his losses in perfection. For the word of our G-d endures forever.

The essential redemption depends on faith [emunah]. And to complete faith, it is impossible to merit except through truth. And to come to truth is through receiving the holy counsels of the truly righteous Tzaddikim. And this is the aspect of the totality of the Torah — the 613 counsels of the Torah [taryag itin d'oraisa]. And this is the aspect of the great miracle of the exodus from Egypt. For at that time it was still before the giving of the Torah — which is those 613 counsels aforementioned. For since the defilements of Egypt still clung to them very greatly — therefore it was still impossible for them to receive the light of the holy counsels. Because of the defilement of the serpent — which is the aspect of the counsel of the wicked — that still clung to them. And naturally, when one does not merit to receive the light of the holy counsels — then one is distant from truth and from faith. And how can there be a redemption?!

And G-d made His kindness wondrous to us — and shined upon us a great and very awesome light that was not in a gradual manner. That is, He shined upon us the light of the very essence of truth before we merited to receive the holy counsels. And through the light of truth we merited great faith — through which the redemption came. And this is the aspect of the great and awesome expanded consciousness [moichin gedolim v'nora'im] alluded to in the commandment of eating matzah — that is, the aspect of the greatness of the illumination of the very essence of truth that shines upon us then. For the essential purpose of the greatness of the expanded consciousness is truth — which is the sum total of all the holy expanded consciousnesses in the world. And therefore chametz is then forbidden with a severe prohibition. For a person's eating corresponds to da'as — for the brain and the da'as are commensurate with the eating. As explained elsewhere. And all the holy counsels are the aspect of the leavening of the holy brain [chamitz hamoi'ach d'kedushah] — for counsel must be [developed] with settled mind and deliberateness, until the matter is well leavened. But corresponding to this there is also the aspect of the leavening of the brain of the sitra achra — which are evil counsels and thoughts and bad ideas that are against the holy Torah. And therefore the yetzer hara is called the she'or sheba'isah [the leaven in the dough]. And there is no wisdom and no counsel to stand against it — except through the holy counsels of the holy Torah. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "I created the yetzer hara — I created the Torah as its antidote."

And since at that time it was still before the receiving of the Torah — and it was impossible to wait until they received the light of truth through the holy counsels in a gradual and orderly manner, because the defilement of the serpent — which is the aspect of the counsel of the wicked — still clung to them — therefore chametz and she'or were then forbidden. For then the chametz is the aspect of the leavening of the brain of the sitra achra. Rather, we must receive then the light of truth itself — before it is leavened and clothed in the aspect of counsels. And therefore on Shavuos — when we merited to receive the 613 counsels and the defilement of the serpent ceased from us — then the chametz was sweetened and repaired with great holiness, to the point that specifically then two loaves of leavened bread [shtai halechem] are brought.

And this matter of the exodus from Egypt occurs in every person and at every time. For whenever a person is sunk, G-d forbid, in the exile of the soul — there are times when a person is so sunken that it is impossible to reveal to him any holy counsel as to how to emerge from the darkness and the exile. For whatever holy counsel may be given to him — the sitra achra overpowers it and corrupts it through its evil counsels — which are the aspect of the defilement of the serpent. But when G-d has compassion upon a person and wishes to bring within him an awakening to teshuvah — then G-d illuminates in his mind the light of the very essence of truth before the holy counsels are revealed. Through this very truth he is drawn after holiness with great yearning and merits faith. And through this he draws close to the truly righteous Tzaddikim and walks in the path of their counsel. And then he receives the true truth of the true Tzadik and of the holy Torah — through receiving the holy counsels within which the light of truth is clothed. For the counsel of the Tzaddikim is the aspect of "all of it seed of truth."

And this too is the aspect of eating maror [bitter herbs] — which is in remembrance of the subjugation and exile. For one must endure great bitterness before meriting to extract the holy counsels from the grip of the sitra achra — which is the aspect of the counsel of the serpent — that confuses all the holy counsels and literally makes life bitter. Which is the aspect of: "And they made their lives bitter with mortar and with bricks" [Exodus 1:14] — b'chomra d'shme'ata ulivun halachta [in the difficulty of the studied law and the clarification of the halacha] — for all of this is the aspect of the extraction and clarification of the holy counsels, which are the sum total of all the halachos in the Torah — the 613 counsels. And it is called counsel and wisdom [etzah v'sushiyah]. But through the illumination of the very essence of truth that G-d shined upon us at Pesach — through this all the aforementioned bitterness was nullified through the illumination of the great expanded consciousness — the aspect of the light of truth — which is the aspect of matzah as above.

Wine elevates the mind above its level. And therefore there are two aspects to it: if one is worthy [zachah] — it becomes a head [rosh]; if not worthy — it becomes impoverished [rash]. For it is impossible to drink wine in great holiness except when one merits the repair of the bris — through which one merits holy counsels and truth and faith. And then one can merit through the wine — that his brain will be elevated and his da'as expanded, until he ascends to the root of da'as: which is the aspect of the root of Torah and commandments — where he is above all the commandments of the Torah. And all the commandments receive their vitality and illumination from there. And when he ascends there, he is inflamed more and more and strengthened more and more to fulfill the commandments of the Torah — because he draws upon himself the light of the root of the commandments.

But in the reverse, G-d forbid — when one has not yet merited the aforementioned aspects, and his faith is not yet complete — then through the drinking of wine and intoxication one can greatly corrupt — to the point that all evil paths seem to him like a plain, G-d forbid. As it is written: "For he sets his eye upon the cup — he walks in upright paths" [Proverbs 23:31] — meaning: seemingly straight to him. For since his brain has been elevated above the vessels of his own brain — he no longer sees according to his own level all the warnings of the commandments of Moshe — [Moshe] — our master. And as is explained elsewhere on the verse: "Lest he drink and forget what has been decreed" [Proverbs 31:5].

And therefore at Pesach — when the light of truth itself is revealed above the level of the expanded consciousness — that is, before truth is clothed in the counsels as above — therefore the obligation is to drink four cups of wine. For now, specifically through the wine, the brain is elevated and one receives the light of truth itself above the vessels of the expanded consciousness. And through this the holy faith is completed. And through this the blemish of Adam the first is repaired — as our Sages of blessed memory said: "She squeezed grapes and gave it to him." And the blemish of Noach — as it is said of him: "And he drank of the wine, etc." — as explained in the inner teachings.

And therefore they are four cups — corresponding to the four expressions of redemption. For the essential redemption depends on faith as above. And the four cups correspond to the four aspects — which are: faith, and prayer, and miracles, and the Land of Israel. Each cup corresponding to one aspect individually, as explained in the inner teachings.

In every generation a person is obligated to see himself as if he personally left Egypt. For this aspect is in every person and at every time. For the essential bitterness of the exile for every person is the aspect of the entanglement of money and livelihood. And the essential redemption of the soul for every person is commensurate with how much he merits to draw close to the truly righteous Tzaddikim — through which he breaks the desire for money and merits to be happy with his portion. Through feeling his poverty in all aspects: body and soul and money. And through this he merits the aspect of redemption — the aspect of holy wealth. Until through this he can merit even actual great physical wealth. And this is the essential complete redemption that will come through our righteous Mashiach — when all wealth will be returned to holiness for Israel. For they will all be Tzaddikim then. And as is explained in many verses — the great wealth that will be then. And all this will be merited specifically through the bitter poverty they endured in this exile. And even then — when they emerge from this exile and merit wealth — even so they will not forget their poverty and will not become arrogant. Rather, they will consider themselves poor — as it is written: "And a poor and lowly people will take refuge in Him" [Zephaniah 3:12]. And also Mashiach himself is called ani [poor] and "riding upon a donkey" [Zechariah 9:9]. For the essential true wealth — spiritually and physically — is merited through true poverty and lowliness as above.

One who wishes to enter the service of G-d — this is truly the aspect of the exodus from Egypt. For the essential exodus from Egypt is going out from impurity to purity — from the impurity and defilement of Pharaoh and Egypt to the holiness of Israel. As it is written: "When you bring forth the people from Egypt, you shall serve G-d, etc." [Exodus 3:12]. And this is necessarily what passes over a person at every time and in every generation — as our Sages of blessed memory said: "In every generation a person is obligated to see himself as if he personally left Egypt." For all that passed over Israel at the exodus from Egypt, and the receiving of the Torah, and thereafter — and all the wars to conquer the Land of Israel — and all that passed over us afterwards — all of it, precisely and exactly, passes over every person who wishes to merit the life of eternity. For necessarily, many kinds of countless battles will pass over him. And every time he wishes to awaken and strengthen himself in the service of G-d — they intensify each time more, especially in the beginning. Which is the aspect of: "Let the work be heavier upon the men, etc." — said at the beginning of the redemption from Egypt. For when the sitra achra sees that a true Tzadik — in the aspect of Moshe — comes and wishes to bring the person of Israel out from the exile of his soul — it provokes and intensifies against him more and more, and makes this world and the desires and the livelihood heavier upon him — until it is difficult for him to move from his place to return to G-d.

But the way of Israel the holy people — who hold the craft of their ancestors in their hands — is that every time they cry out to G-d. And through this they subdue each time Pharaoh and his forces — which are the sitra achra and its sects. But even though they subdue them — even so, they return and intensify every single time. And so, time after time, many times — as we saw with Pharaoh: that every time some plague came upon him he yielded somewhat, and afterwards he hardened his heart and returned and intensified. And even after the entire exodus from Egypt was complete, he returned and gathered his forces and pursued after them and caught up with them at the sea. And then Israel was in great distress and in great straits — as our Sages of blessed memory said on the verse: "My dove in the clefts of the rock, etc." [Song of Songs 2:14]. And likewise precisely so it passes over every person at every time, each according to his level.

And this is the aspect of the kriyas Yam Suf [splitting of the Red Sea] — the aspect of: "And the Children of Israel came within the sea upon dry land" [Exodus 14:22]. That is: when the insolent waters — which are the aspect of evil thoughts, etc., which are called literally the depths of the sea — intensify, G-d forbid, and there is nowhere to flee — neither forward nor backward nor to any side. Exactly as was the case then at the splitting of the Sea — the sea was storming before them, the Egyptians were behind them, and on their sides were wild beasts and serpents and scorpions. When then the soul of the person of Israel is in great distress and great straits — then there is no remedy except to cry out to G-d. And then G-d sends him a great strengthening in his heart and his mind — not to look behind him at all at the confusing thoughts, which are the aspect of the depths of the sea aforementioned. Rather, he should rush like a warrior to run the path — to pass through all the thoughts and confusions, etc. — and to walk in the holy path upon which he is engaged: in Torah and prayer, etc.

And this is the aspect of: "Speak to the Children of Israel and let them journey forth" [Exodus 14:15] — that they should go their way and leap into the sea — and not think and not look behind them at all. And so they did — they entered into the sea up to their nostrils, as our Sages of blessed memory said. That is, they did not look at all at the insolent rushing waters — rather, they walked in confidence upon their way and engaged in their service in Torah and prayer within the intensification of the roaring crashing waves, which are the thoughts and the confusions. And they did not look behind them at all — rather, they did what they had to do. And then — when G-d saw the firmness of their heart, that they did not abandon their service through any confusion in the world, even though they had already entered the water up to their nostrils — then G-d had compassion upon them and split the sea before them. "And the Children of Israel came within the sea upon dry land." For so it is: when one strengthens oneself with great strengthening to go in one's way in prayer and service — and not to look behind at all — then suddenly they are nullified by themselves entirely, exactly like the sea that was nullified before Israel and turned into dry land.

In the matter of Pesach Sheini [the second Passover] — it is alluded to that there is no despair in the world whatsoever. For even one who is impure or is on a very far road [derech rechokah] from G-d — and is unable to bring the offering of G-d at its appointed time — that is, does not merit to always serve His service in proper order, at its time and season, as is fitting for a person of Israel — even so, if he does not despair of himself because of this and goes to the true Tzadik — who is in the aspect of Moshe — to seek G-d. And asks and requests: "Why should we be diminished from not bringing the offering of G-d, etc.?" [Numbers 9:7]. For even though I have defiled my soul and been distanced from G-d — even so, I ask for counsel and a means as to how to draw close to G-d at least from now on. For certainly there is a counsel for me too as to how to draw close to G-d. Then G-d has compassion upon him — and he merits through this the ultimate elevation. And merits through this to add a Torah portion [parshah b'Torah]. For through seeking and searching for "where is the place of His glory?" — through this one merits the subsequent revelation of the Torah — [of the Torah] — as explained elsewhere.

Even though in truth one must hurry and hasten very — [very] — greatly to rescue one's soul. And especially one who has already stumbled and been caught in what he has been caught, G-d protect us — even so, it is — [it is] — impossible to press the moment. And one must wait and wait — until G-d looks down from Heaven and sees. But even so, even within the time of the waiting and the delay — it is forbidden to remove one's mind from this. Rather, one must hope and anticipate and look forward and count and tell the days — and long and yearn at every time: when will he merit the day of the complete salvation of his soul?

And this is the aspect of the Sefirah [Counting of the Omer] — where we do nothing except count the days and the weeks. And through this we draw upon ourselves the holiness of the renewed receiving of the Torah each year. That is, through this very aspect aforementioned — that we want and desire and yearn to receive the Torah. And according to the strength of our will and our strong yearning — certainly we would want to receive it with alacrity immediately and at once. But in truth it is impossible to press the moment — and it is necessary to wait until — [until] — the fiftieth day. But even so, even now it is forbidden to forget and to remove one's mind from this, G-d forbid. Which is the aspect of why we count the days — for the counting shows the very — [very] — essence of the longing and the pining — [and the pining]. Like one who yearns and craves for some matter — then the way is to count the days until he attains his longing. Likewise, we count and reckon the days and the weeks — which shows the essence of the longing and the strong will we have for the receiving of the Torah.

And therefore in truth all of Israel is accustomed to fulfill the commandment of counting the Omer with great awakening and great yearning toward G-d. And through this we merit to draw in perfection the aspect of hot words like coals of fire — in the aspect of: "For love is as strong as death, etc." [Song of Songs 8:6]. That is, through the greatness of the holy love and yearning aforementioned — one merits: "its flashes are flashes of fire" [Song of Songs 8:6]. And through this one merits the receiving of the Torah in the aspect of: "And you heard His words from within the fire" [Deuteronomy 4:36] — as mentioned above.

All the days of the year one must prepare himself for Rosh Hashanah — which is the Day of Judgment. For the essential thing is Rosh Hashanah. For just as a person must prepare himself all the days of his life for the great and awesome Day of Judgment in the future — likewise in the particular, he must prepare himself all the days of the year for Rosh Hashanah — which is the Day of Judgment. For it is awesome and dreadful, etc. And especially one must begin and prepare himself when he sees the days approaching — which is from the fifteenth of Av onwards. For then begins the sweetening of the sin of the Golden Calf and the sin of the Spies — through which, in all of this, the holy memory [zikaron d'kedushah] was blemished. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "From the day the Tablets were broken, forgetting descended upon the world." And on the fifteenth of Av began the sweetening of the breaking of the Tablets — and the illumination of the forty days of favor begins to shine. For then they subsequently received on Yom Kippur the second Tablets — which merited the aspect of the repair of memory. And therefore our Sages of blessed memory said: "No days were as good for Israel as the fifteenth of Av and Yom Kippur." For on the fifteenth of Av begins to shine the illumination from the second Tablets given on Yom Kippur. And therefore on the fifteenth of Av the sin of the Spies was also repaired — for on it the desert generation ceased dying, as our Sages of blessed memory said. And therefore from the fifteenth of Av one must begin to rise at midnight — which is the aspect of the repair of memory.

And afterwards during the month of Elul one engages in this more and more. And all of Israel is awakened then and remembers G-d and the World to Come. And this is the aspect of the blowing of the shofar throughout the month of Elul. For the shofar is the aspect of remembrance — as it is written: "And it shall be for you a remembrance" [Numbers 10:10]. And the essential repair of memory flows on Rosh Hashanah — when the essential commandment of the shofar is performed. Which is the Day of Remembrance [yom hazikaron]. For it is the first of the Ten Days of Repentance — and one must draw upon himself the aforementioned remembrance. Through which comes the essential teshuvah. And for this purpose one must journey to the Tzaddikim for Rosh Hashanah. For this is the essential occupation of the Tzaddikim always — to remind us of our eternal purpose in the World to Come, and to teach us counsels and straight paths to merit this. And especially the Tzaddikim engage in this on Rosh Hashanah, as explained in the inner teachings.

And this remembrance is in the general and in the particular. And this is the secret of the year [shanah] and the awakening of the year [his'orrus hashanah] at Rosh Hashanah. For the shanah is the aspect of remembrance of the World to Come in the general — for then the soul ascends to the aspect of the World to Come. And afterwards — in the awakening of the year — then one must engage in this in the particular. And afterwards — on Yom Kippur — then comes the completion of the repair of the remembrance. And therefore the second Tablets were given then. And the High Priest entered on it into the innermost chamber, as explained in the inner teachings.

And afterwards one enters the sukkah — which is the encompassing clouds of glory [ananei kavod] that protect us so that the evil eye no longer has dominion over us — which is the aspect of the husk of Amalek. So as not to blemish again, G-d forbid, the holy memory we drew upon ourselves in these days — especially on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur. And this is the aspect of the joy one multiplies on Sukkos — in order to repair also through this the aspect of — [the aspect of] — the imagination [hamedameh]. For all of this is the aspect of the repair of memory aforementioned. And therefore one then takes the four species of the lulav. And the holy Zohar explains that through this we take Him, blessed be He, as it were, in our hands — that is, we draw upon ourselves the remembrance in the particular: which is the aspect of the hints whereby G-d contracts Himself from the Infinite to the infinite [me'ain sof ad ain techlis] in thought, speech, and action each day — and hints to the person everywhere and at all times to draw close to Him. Which is the aspect of the wavings that are waved to all directions. That is, we draw upon ourselves these hints aforementioned.

One must journey to the truly righteous Tzaddikim for Rosh Hashanah. For only they can draw the paths of teshuvah in perfection. And the essential [need] is to sweeten the force of the judgment of Rosh Hashanah and to draw joy upon oneself — through which comes the essential repair of teshuvah. For even though the shofar of Rosh Hashanah is the aspect of a broken heart — for the penitent must have a broken heart. Which is the aspect of: "If the shofar is blown in the city, will the people not tremble?" [Amos 3:6]. But after the broken heart one must come to joy. And this is the aspect of: "Fortunate is the people who know the teruah, etc." [Psalms 89:16]. And adjacent to it: "In Your name they will rejoice all the day, etc." [Psalms 89:17].

The essential holiness of a person is when he confines himself within his home and his chamber — in the aspect of: "Go, my people, enter your chambers, etc." [Isaiah 26:20]. And it is said: "Walk humbly with your G-d" [Micah 6:8]. And this is the aspect of the praise said of Torah scholars: "All the glory of the king's daughter is within" [Psalms 45:14]. For the essential splendor and holiness of a person is when he sits within his home — where the essential flow of holiness resides. But outside is the domain of the dominion of the outer forces.

And therefore it would have been fitting that a person always sit within his home. But a person is necessarily compelled to go outside as well every single time. And this is the aspect of ail v'nafak [entering and exiting]. For even though it would have been fitting for a person to always be attached to holiness in the aspect of entry — even so, the essential perfection of holiness is specifically when a person merits to be ail v'nafak. For a person necessarily passes through many ascents and descents every single day. And when he merits to be expert in the halacha [baki b'halacha] — in the aspect of baki b'ail, baki b'nafak [expert in entering, expert in exiting] — to fulfill as it is written: "If I ascend to the heavens — there You are, and if I make my bed in the abyss — behold You are there" [Psalms 139:8] — to hold fast to G-d always with a strong bond, both in ascent and in descent — then he merits to elevate even external places and lower levels all to holiness. And then the descent is the ultimate purpose of the ascent.

And this is the aspect of the necessity of leaving the home into the outside every single time. For when one goes outside — which is the aspect of nafak — where the dominion of the outer forces resides — and when one remembers G-d even there and cleaves to Him, blessed be He — then he extracts the holiness of external places and elevates everything to holiness. And this is the aspect of: "When you sit in your home and when you walk on the way" [Deuteronomy 6:7] — the aspect of ail v'nafak.

And this is the aspect of Israel walking in the desert — which is a place of outer forces, a place of serpent and fiery snake and scorpion — in order to subdue the sitra achra and to extract the holiness also from there, in the aspect of: "Fortunate is one who enters and exits." And then specifically — when they walk in the desert in outer places, which is the aspect of nafak — and when they merit to find G-d there — then specifically G-d hovers over Israel with very lofty holiness. Which is the aspect of the encompassing clouds of glory that Israel merited in the desert. Which are the aspect of sukkah — the aspect of the mother who hovers over her children [ima d'mesachcha al banin]. Which is a very lofty holiness that hovers and protects over a person specifically at the time when he is in the aspect of nafak — in order to guard him and rescue him lest he fall there, G-d — [G-d] — forbid. And helps him to subdue the sitra achra and to extract specifically from there the holiness. It is thus found that specifically through the aspect of nafak one merits a very great ascent — to the aspect of sukkah. Which is the aspect of descent being the ultimate purpose of ascent aforementioned.

And this is the aspect of the commandment of sukkah — which G-d caused us to merit at the beginning of the year, at the beginning of the teshuvah. Which must be in the aspect of ail v'nafak specifically. And the aspect of ail is fulfilled on Rosh Hashanah and the Ten Days of Repentance and Yom Kippur. And afterwards one must fulfill also the aspect of nafak — which is the aspect of the completion [tamah]: that one goes out from the home to sit in the sukkah — to show that when a person is in the aspect of nafak and seeks and — [seeks and] — searches even there to cleave to G-d — then specifically he merits very lofty holiness, the aspect of sukkah. Which is the aspect of the encompassing lights [makifim] that guard and protect the person then — when he is in the aspect of nafak.

And through the commandment of sukkah we merit throughout the year to do — [to do] — complete teshuvah in the aspect of ail v'nafak. And at every time we are in the aspect of nafak — the sukkas shalom [shelter of peace] protects us like a mother protecting her child from falling, G-d forbid, when he walks in a dangerous place. And this is what we request specifically at night — which is the aspect of nafak, corresponding to the attribute of day — "and spread over us the shelter of Your peace." For then specifically the shelter of peace guards [us]. For the shelter of peace always guards a person at every time of danger where protection is needed — then the shelter of peace guards. And this is the aspect of: "For He will hide me in His sukkah on the day of evil" [Psalms 27:5] — specifically on the day of evil — which is the aspect of nafak — that is, at the time a person falls from his service. And when he merits to strengthen himself and not despair of himself even then — then the shelter of peace guards us as above.

All the decrees, G-d protect us, derive from sins. And the general repair [tikun hakelali] of all sins is the repair of the bris. And likewise the general repair of speech is the praise of the Tzaddikim. And the general repair of commerce is tzedakah [charity]. And this is the aspect of: "Teshuvah, prayer, and charity avert the evil of the decree" — which correspond to: fasting, voice, and money [tzom, kol, mamon]. For fasting is the aspect of the repair of the bris as above. Prayer is the aspect of the abundance of prayers and praises that one multiplies to G-d on Yom Kippur. And tzedakah is the aspect of the general repair of commerce as above.

A person must know and believe that G-d makes new things at every time — and no day is like another, how much more so that no year is like another. And in every day — and especially in every single year — everything is renewed entirely. And certainly G-d and the Tzaddikim will complete what they have begun. And if in the meanwhile what passes over us in the general and the particular passes over us — and the sitra achra and the baal davar spreads lengthwise and widthwise every single time — even so G-d helps us every day. And especially each year — when we receive the holiness of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur until Simchas Torah. And then the Torah is completed and we begin it again. And in each year new repairs are completed for each person — in a manner that every person can always be renewed for the good. As long as he believes in the truth: that G-d in His goodness each day always renews the act of creation. Especially each and every year. Until in the end the repair will be completed in perfection through our righteous Mashiach — may he come speedily in our days.

At the resting place of the Tzaddikim in their holy graves — there the holiness of the Throne of Glory [kise hakavod] is drawn — which is their inheritance. As it is written: "And a glorious throne shall He cause them to inherit" [I Samuel 2:8]. And therefore there are included all the places of every single person — and every single person can find his place there, until he merits through this to return to G-d. Because there shines the holiness of the aspect of mekomo shel olam [the place of the world] — which is the root of all places. And there every person can find the beginning and the starting point from which he must begin to return to G-d. And for this reason people travel to the graves of the Tzaddikim on the eve of Rosh Hashanah.

On Rosh Hashanah G-d has compassion upon us and judges us to the scale of merit — each person according to his place. And through this we truly enter into the scale of merit — until through this we merit to cry out to G-d from the depths of the heart and to return in teshuvah before Him, blessed be He. And afterwards — on Hoshana Rabbah, at the end of Sukkos — through meriting to sit in the sukkah, which is the aspect of the Throne of Glory, mekomo shel olam — through this all of Israel merits to receive illumination from there. Until we all merit this aspect: to fulfill: "Do not judge your fellow until you have reached his place" [Avos 2:5]. And to know to judge everyone to the scale of merit — even the sinners of Israel — until we merit to bring them all into the scale of merit and to shine upon them the illumination of Rosh Hashanah. That is, that all of them will always find a door and a path of teshuvah in every place they are, at every time.

And the essential door and path is to always cry out to G-d from the depths of the heart — however things may be — and to never despair of the cry. Which is the aspect of the abundance of cries that one multiplies on Hoshana Rabbah — crying out many, many times: Hoshana! And one stays awake the entire night and completes the book of Psalms — which is full of cries and wails and pleas, etc., to G-d. Until there is no person in the world who cannot find himself in the book of Psalms — which encompasses all who come into the world in all generations and at all levels in the world down to the very lowest possible level — and stirs them all to return to G-d. For Psalms is a segula for teshuvah.

And on Hoshana Rabbah we draw this wondrous path — that every person of Israel should merit through the holiness of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur and Sukkos — to judge everything to the scale of merit, and to bring the paths of teshuvah into every single person of Israel: that is, to say Psalms and to cry out to G-d always, however things may be. And likewise one must judge even himself to the scale of merit and fulfill in himself: "Do not judge, etc., until you have reached his place." For certainly even his own place — he does not know from where it is drawn. And whatever passed over him in all his gilgulim [reincarnations], and from where his evil desires and evil thoughts derive, etc. Therefore it is forever forbidden to despair of oneself. For one must fulfill in oneself as well: "Do not be contemptuous of any person" — which is the aspect of the prohibition of bloodshed [shfichus damim], as explained in the inner teachings. For a person is warned against the prohibition of bloodshed also regarding his own soul. As it is written: "But your blood of your own lives, etc." [Genesis 9:5] — and our Sages of blessed memory expounded: "This refers to one who spills his own blood." For even to hold oneself in too much contempt — to the point that he could fall even more through this, G-d forbid — this is certainly a severe prohibition. For one must judge even oneself to the scale of merit — for who knows his own place?

And the essential thing: do not despair yourself of the cry — ever. And cry out and implore before G-d always from the depths of the heart — in the aspect of: "Pour out your heart like water before the face of G-d" [Lamentations 2:19]. Through which we will all merit to return to Him, blessed be He. And all of this we engage in drawing [l'hamshich] on Hoshana Rabbah. And therefore we engage then with the willow branches [aravei nachal] — which allude to the sinners of Israel — to fulfill in them also: "Do not be contemptuous of any person" — and to judge them to the scale of merit. And this is the aspect of what is said on Hoshana Rabbah — Mishneh Torah — which revolves and orbits entirely around this very axis: to warn Israel that in all that passes over them, etc. — even so, they should never despair of themselves from the cry. For G-d will not abandon His people — and His compassion never ends. And after all the sins and provocations with which they provoke before Him, blessed be He, in every generation — even so, the right hand of G-d is exalted. And therefore one can always draw close and return to Him, blessed be He, from whatever place one is.

The essential joining of two things that are very far from one another — which are like two opposites — the essential joining of them is through melody [nigun] — as explained in the inner teachings. And therefore the essential attachment [devekus] to G-d from this very low and physical and lowly world is through melody and song. As one can see plainly: that even a person who is very far from G-d and is on the very lowest rung — even so, most of the time through melody he is awakened toward G-d and reminds himself where he stands in the world. Only one must be careful not to hear melody from wicked and frivolous musicians — who are very commonly found now. For this can harm him, G-d forbid, very greatly. But through melody from people who are truly upright — who direct their hearts in truth toward G-d — or when one plays some melody oneself and his intention is for the sake of Heaven — one can be awakened through this very greatly toward G-d.

For the essential joining and attachment from this world — the physical world — to G-d — who is immeasurably exalted and elevated — especially for one who has sinned and been greatly distanced from his Father in Heaven — is through melody and song. Which is the aspect of all the songs and praises spoken to G-d. And for this reason King David, peace be upon him, composed the entire book of Psalms — which encompasses all ten types of melody. For he is the aspect of Mashiach — who engages in repairing the blemish of the broken Tablets. Through which all the destructions came. And David — who is Mashiach — who engages in repairing this, which is the repair of all the worlds — therefore composed the book of Psalms encompassing all ten types of melody. For through the ten types of melody the broken Tablets are repaired. For through melody for the sake of Heaven — one attaches and joins the heart to G-d from wherever one is. Until one can receive the light of the letters of the Torah — in the aspect of: "write them upon the tablet of your heart" [Proverbs 3:3]. And likewise — commensurate with how much the heart is drawn after G-d — so too there is the power for the Tablets to bear the light of the letters of the Torah. Which is the aspect of the repair of the broken Tablets — which came about through the aspect of the letters flying off, as our Sages of blessed memory said.

And this is the aspect of: "Bind them upon your throat" [Proverbs 3:3] — specifically [davka] — the aspect of the throat and larynx from which the voice emerges. There should be bound in it the words of Torah. That is, his melody should be for the sake of Heaven. And through this: "write them upon the tablet of your heart" — as above. And through this one merits to be saved from the forgetting of Torah — and merits to see the light of Torah in perfection in the aspect of a life-giving remedy [sam chayyim].

The essential of pride is in the aspect of the eyes — as it is written: "haughtiness of eyes" [Proverbs 6:17]. And one who shatters his pride and nullifies himself in the ultimate nullification — through this he merits to look upward with his eyes — to behold the pleasantness of G-d [lachazos b'no'am Hashem]. For it is impossible to ascend from level to level and to look upward as is fitting in perfection — except through the ultimate nullification.

Our Sages of blessed memory said: "The beams of a person's house, his rafters, and the stones of his house testify against him at the time of judgment." And seemingly this is wondrous — and if so, if someone committed a transgression, G-d forbid, outside or in a field where there are no walls [mechitzos] — who testifies against him? But in truth the essential witnesses are the aspect of the walls [mechitzos] of the house — both in the physical and in the spiritual. For all transgressions and all desires come through the blemish of the eyes — through going after one's eyes. Especially the desire for licentiousness — whose root is specifically through the sight — [sight] — of the eyes. As it is written: "And you shall not go astray after your hearts and after your eyes, etc." [Numbers 15:39] — as our Sages of blessed memory expounded. And the essential [blemish] is through the sight of the eyes of the thought [ainei hamachshavah] — for in whatever a person looks with his thought — whether for good or for the reverse — this is also called sight.

And a person must guard his eyes — physically and spiritually — not to look, G-d forbid, at anything that brings to improper thoughts. And in what he is necessarily compelled to see with his eyes — he must be very careful not to allow the eyes of his thought to look and gaze upon this, G-d forbid, until he comes to improper thoughts, G-d forbid. Rather, one must immediately erect the partition [mechitzah] of the brain against this desire. For the brain is an erected partition against this desire. And the choice is in the person's hand — to seize his thought — [his thought] — and to erect — [and to erect] — the partition of the brain and to be saved from this desire. For thought is in the person's hand to redirect it to the straight path. And as is brought elsewhere. And therefore the rafters and the stones of a person's house — which are the partitions — specifically testify against him. For even the physical partitions of a person's house — G-d created them all for the sake of guarding. For G-d created many partitions for the person before his eyes — so that he can guard his eyes from seeing evil, G-d forbid. For He created over the eye two partitions to cover it — which are the eyelashes and eyelids. As our Sages of blessed memory said. And likewise He created the partitions of the houses — within which a person must be hidden most of the time — in order to be guarded from the harm of seeing with the eyes that is outside.

And the essential complete partitions — which are the essential guardianship above all guardianships — are the partitions of the brain [mechitzos hamoi'ach] as above. For even when sitting in the house — one must be careful not to blemish the partitions of the brain — not to come to improper thoughts, G-d forbid. And then — when one guards the partitions of the brain as is fitting — even when necessarily compelled to go out to the marketplace — he will be guarded there too through the partitions of the brain — which are partitions erected against this desire. And therefore one who blemished in some transgression, G-d forbid — which is only through the blemish of the partitions — therefore his rafters and the stones of his house — which are the partitions — testify against him. And therefore the Torah begins with the letter bais [beraishis] — for beraishis alludes to the three colors of the eye and the pupil, as is brought elsewhere. For the essential fulfillment of the Torah is through the guarding of the eyes — through the repair of the partitions — which are the aspect of bais [house] — the aspect of bais of beraishis.

The essential deficiency of livelihood comes from the deficiency of counsel [chisaron ha'etzah]. For all livelihood comes easily when one knows to give oneself counsel as to how to conduct oneself and in what to earn. As it is written: "For it is He who gives you the power to make wealth" [Deuteronomy 8:18] — and the Targum [Onkelos] renders: "For it is He who gives you counsel to acquire wealth." For certainly at every time and at every moment there is some commerce and trade through which one could certainly earn. And if a person truly knew the counsel at every time — which commerce is needed now — certainly he would have livelihood and great wealth. And this is simple and clear.

One who wishes to set his heart upon his ways — to look at his purpose and his eternal end — knows and understands that every single day one needs very many deep counsels to be saved from what one needs to be saved from, each according to his matters. Until he merits to pass the day in peace. For the yetzer hara overpowers a person every single day — and how many causes and adventures pass over a person every single day. And how many and how many deep counsels and great strategies one needs each day — that he merit to be saved from the cruel murderers and ambushers who stand over him every day: which are the yetzer hara and its forces. And one must every single day cry out abundantly from the depths — the very depths of the heart — [the heart] — in the aspect of: "From the depths I call You, G-d" [Psalms 130:1] — the aspect of: "Their heart cried out to G-d" [Lamentations 2:18]. Until one merits to draw deep counsels from the true Tzadik — which are the aspect of: "Deep waters — counsel in the heart of a man, and a man of understanding draws it up" [Proverbs 20:5]. So that he may merit to know to give himself counsel in every matter in a manner that will bring him true and eternal success.

And for this King David, peace be upon him, cried out much: "How long shall I take counsel in my soul, etc.?" [Psalms 13:3]. And it is written: "With Your counsel You will guide me" [Psalms 73:24]. And it is written: "I will bless G-d who advises me, etc." [Psalms 16:7]. And for this our Sages of blessed memory ordained to pray each day: "And repair us with good counsel from before You."

The saying of our Sages of blessed memory is known: "In the path a person wishes to go — he is led along it." And from this come all the corrupted counsels — where it seems to him that they come from G-d — or that the Tzadik gave him this counsel. And in truth it all comes from himself. As it is written: "The folly of a person perverts his way, etc." [Proverbs 19:3]. For as one asks the Tzadik — so he answers. Therefore one who truly wishes to have consideration for himself must beg greatly in many supplications both G-d and the truly righteous Tzaddikim — that they place their heart fully upon what is being done with him and have compassion upon him in truth — in a manner that they give him a true counsel through which he will succeed in truth in prevailing in truth.

Sometimes a person falls into so many doubts and divided counsels — that it is impossible for him in any way to know the truth as to how to conduct himself. And everything he strives to find as a complete counsel — his counsel is confused every single time. For now he has concluded in his mind with clear proofs that he must conduct himself in such and such a manner. And in the meanwhile a different view arises in his mind — until his first counsel is entirely overturned. And there arise in his mind views that he must conduct himself in the complete opposite of what he had previously thought. And this is the aspect of the divided counsels aforementioned. And sometimes the division of counsel intensifies so greatly — that he does not know in any way to decide the counsel to one side or the other.

And when a person sees in himself that he has been lying in this darkness for a long time and does not know any counsel as to how to emerge from what he needs to emerge from — and his counsel is very divided, G-d forbid — then this itself is his remedy: that he cry out to G-d about this very thing itself — about having fallen so far that he does not know the complete counsel as to how to emerge from darkness to light. For certainly there is no despair in the world at all. And certainly even in his place there are counsels as to how to emerge from darkness to light, from bad to good. Only that through his sins they have been hidden from him — in the aspect of: "Who is this who darkens counsel with words, etc.?" [Job 38:2]. And therefore his remedy is: that he know at least the truth — that he has fallen so far and been distanced so far that he does not know any counsel. And let him cry out about this itself to G-d — that He show him the counsel and the path as to how to truly conduct himself. As King David, peace be upon him, cried out much about this — for in truth even the very great Tzaddikim of very high stature — even upon them there pass — [counsels] — divided counsels in their matters and in their conduct. And as is understood from what King David, peace be upon him, cried out: "How long shall I take counsel in my soul, etc.?" — from which it is understood that greatly divided counsels passed over him. How much more so and certainly those of lower worth — how much more so those caught in the prison of desires and improper thoughts, etc. etc., G-d protect us — who must know and believe that certainly in every place they are, there is a counsel and a strategy as to how to emerge and return from there. Only they do not know the counsel — and their counsel is always divided. And therefore their remedy is: that they know the truth — that they do not know any counsel — and pray about this much to G-d. And then they can merit that the descent be the ultimate purpose of the ascent, as explained in the inner teachings.

One must banish sleep from his eyes and his eyelids — to wander and seek and multiply prayer and supplication, that he merit to find the Tzadik who can heal him and bring within him the attainment of G-dliness, and rescue his soul from destruction. And for this one must break the sleep and rise at midnight and weep and cry out greatly over the destruction of the Temple and over the passing of the Tzaddikim — which is twice as hard as the destruction of the Temple. Until he merits even now to find the true — [true] — rebbe and leader, who can bring within him the knowledge of His blessed G-dliness. Through which all his lacks will be filled and all afflictions nullified and everything repaired.

The great Tzadik aforementioned — who engages in drawing close those who are distant, in whom the baal davar and his forces have seized with greatest force — descends in the very depth of his wisdom so far toward them, until it appears as if he is performing acts of youthfulness. For he speaks mundane conversation with them and eats and drinks with them — and sometimes even plays and jokes with them. And all his intention — to draw them close to G-d through this.

There is great virtue in being with the Tzadik at a time when there is a large gathering of many people of Israel with him. For certainly every single particular person is very, very far from the holiness of the Tzadik of the generation. And it is impossible to receive [illumination] from him except through the collective of Israel — through which his great illumination is drawn. And then every single particular person can also receive his illumination individually.

That teshuvah is effective for all sins — this is only from the side of chesed [kindness]. And for the sin of wasting seed [hotzo'as zera l'vatolo] our Sages of blessed memory said that teshuvah is not effective for it — for such is fitting for it, as explained in the inner teachings. But in truth there is nothing that stands before teshuvah. Only the essential repair is through the Tzadik of the generation. For he can awaken and draw upon him new chesed — until this too will be repaired.

In every generation there are many truly righteous Tzaddikim. But there is truth above truth — for certainly the level and stature of all Tzaddikim is not equal. And the greater the stature and level of the Tzaddikim — certainly his truth is greater and he extracts more. For the essential thing is truth. Until in every generation there is a true Tzadik who is the aspect of the point of truth among the Tzaddikim. Only because of the intensification of the substitutions and exchanges — through this it is very difficult to know where the truth is. For most of the time the baal davar provokes even the Tzaddikim themselves and introduces great controversy between them — to dispute this true Tzadik who is the aspect of the point of truth among the Tzaddikim. And it seems to them as if this specific Tzadik is the one who deviates, G-d forbid, from the path of truth.

And from this came the aspect of the controversy of the tribes against Yosef — until "as a slave was Yosef sold" [Psalms 105:17]. And through this the matter rolled on, and our ancestors descended to Egypt and were slaves there. And likewise the controversy of Shaul — who pursued David for no cause. And as we find in many, many generations. Especially in these generations in the footsteps of the Mashiach — when the accusation and the controversy intensified even among the Tzaddikim — until one does not know where the truth is. And therefore one must pray to G-d much about this as above.

This repair that the Tzadik — in the aspect of Moshe — engages in: to elevate from forced apostasy [shmad] to will [ratzon] — this is also needed by every single person according to his level. For even the upright — when they sometimes turn away from G-d — this is considered idol worship [avodah zarah] in the aspect of shmad, G-d protect us. As our Sages of blessed memory said regarding: "And you will turn away and serve other gods" [Deuteronomy 11:16]. And the essential aspect of idolatry and shmad is the desire for money and the entanglement and bitterness of livelihood. For the adversary and the baal davar brings down each person's mind to naturalism [tiv'iyus] — and wishes to distance him from faith in Providence and the Supreme Will. And because of this one always worries about money and livelihood. And there are those who have much money and desire more and more. And all of this is the aspect of shmad. For all idol worship is embedded in money, as explained elsewhere.

And the repair for this is to bind oneself to the truly righteous Tzaddikim of the generation — in the aspect of Moshe — and to multiply in holy tzedakah for the sake of Heaven, and not to be boastful, G-d forbid. And through this the illumination of the will is drawn from the aspect of Moshe who has departed — and is encompassed in the root of the will — ra'ava d'ra'avin [the will of all wills]. Until through this the holy will shines upon them in every kind of darkness to elevate them from there — [from there] — so that through this they ascend from shmad to ratzon.

Every person well knows — how many and how many times pass over him — spiritually and physically — in body and soul and money, etc. And how many and how many wondrous salvations G-d helps him each and every time. Especially in the matter of the holiness of his Judaism — which is the essential thing. And at every time and every time that passes over a person — whether in good or in hardship, whether in ascent or in descent — through all of them the Tzadik illuminates, so that Israel know what counsels to take and by what to keep themselves alive at every time — each according to the time that passes over him. In a manner that they will remain standing and will never fall or be distanced.

And the essential [means] is: through binding all the times that pass over them to the last time — which is the time of receiving the reward of every person of Israel. At that time every person will merit according to his service the illumination of an overflowing will toward G-d — with a wondrous and awesome yearning. Which is the aspect of: "As now it will be said of Yaakov and of Israel: what has G-d wrought?" [Numbers 23:23] — as explained in the inner teachings. And to this time one must bind all the times that pass over him in this world. For the essential strengthening is through the will [ratzon] — that however things are and whatever passes over him — at the very least he should strengthen himself with a strong will toward G-d. For the good will in itself is very precious and important. And through this he will be awakened and will strengthen himself to always pray to G-d and to multiply the recitation of Psalms and supplications and many requests and hisbodidus — to pour out his heart like water before G-d — until G-d looks down from Heaven and sees — and shines upon him the true holy da'as to nullify the spirit of folly and to return from all sins and to draw close to G-d.

The essential [work of the] yetzer hara — which intensifies in every generation — is to hide and conceal the true Tzadik of this very generation. As is plainly visible: the essential controversy is against the Tzadik of that very generation. And afterwards — in the days that come — the world acknowledges also this Tzadik and says that he was certainly a Tzadik. Only they dispute the Tzadik of this very generation. As we saw regarding the controversy that existed against the Arizal, of blessed memory, in his own days — and afterwards all acknowledged the holiness of the Arizal and disputed the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory — and so in every generation. And all of this — because the essential clarification [birur] of the imagination — through which one merits complete faith — is specifically through this very true Tzadik of this very generation.

And therefore the baal davar allows itself to spread lengthwise and widthwise to hide and conceal this specific Tzadik. And therefore every person must strive and draw close to the true Tzadik of this very generation — specifically. In order to merit through him specifically the perfection of the clarification of faith — as is needed for this very generation and time and moment — specifically now.

One who separates himself from the Tzadik — he is the aspect of a dry tree [etz yaveish]. For even if he innovates some innovation in Torah — it is not considered the making of fruit at all. For it is impossible to succeed in Torah and to make true fruit — except when one binds oneself to the true Tzadik. Through which one merits good longings, and good deeds, and true Torah innovations.

One who wishes to have consideration for his life — to rescue his soul from eternal death — and to be saved from the aspect of death [sitra d'musa], which is the aspect of heresies [kefirot] — and to merit complete faith, which is the very essence of life — must journey and come to the Tzaddikim and those attached to them. Which is the secret of the forty-eight cities of refuge [arei miklat] — in which the priests and the Levites dwelt. And where the killer was required to flee and escape. And these forty-eight cities correspond to the forty-eight words of the verse of Shma Yisroel — which is the foundation of the holy faith.

Our Sages of blessed memory said: "Make for yourself a teacher, and acquire for yourself a friend." And it is brought in the sacred books that this alludes to the reed [kaneh] and the quill [kulmus] with which the holy books are written. And this: "Make for yourself a teacher" — and if you cannot find him, then the remedy is through: "and acquire for yourself a friend" — that is, through the holy books written with a reed [kaneh] — bind them — [bind them] — to yourself and study them well. And through this you will be able to know who is the true teacher.

The virtue of the graves of the Tzaddikim — for they are dwellers of the dust [shochnei ofor]. Who even in their lifetimes made themselves neighbors to dust — as our Sages of blessed memory said. And through this they have the aspect of the drawing power that dust has — that is, they have the power to draw toward themselves the holiness of His blessed G-dliness and to draw the entire world toward the holiness of His blessed service. And how much more so now — after the passing — when they are literally dwellers of the dust. And then at the place of the burial of the Tzadik — the dust there is in the aspect of the dust of the Land of Israel — holy soil [admas kodesh]. In the aspect of: "the righteous shall inherit the land" [Psalms 37:29] — as explained elsewhere. And therefore it is easy to truly awaken there to His blessed service — and to strengthen the drawing power of holiness over the compelling power.

The great virtue of the graves of the Tzaddikim — for there everyone can be repaired. Even one who is between two [forces of the] adversary, G-d forbid — the great Tzadik can extract him from there — when one comes to his holy grave and wishes to return in complete teshuvah. For the death of the great Tzadik is very high and elevated and exalted. And then specifically he intensifies with all his strength to complete what he needs to complete for the benefit of the souls of Israel. For the death of the Tzadik is the aspect of prayer in the aspect of judgment [b'ves din] — for the great ba'al ko'ach [master of power] prays — and the sitra achra swallows it. And the prayer — since it is very holy and came from a great ba'al ko'ach — the sitra achra does not have the power to swallow it entirely. Rather, on the contrary — the prayer stands in its throat [b'tzavoroh] — until the sitra achra is compelled through this to vomit and expel and return all the holinesses it has swallowed — including the very essence of its vitality.

And this is the secret of the repairs and extractions that were done until now through the death of the ten martyrs [asarah harugei malchus] — as is brought in the sacred writings. And in truth the death of all the Tzaddikim is the aspect of mesiras nefesh [self-sacrifice] for the sanctification of G-d's Name. Especially the death of the Tzaddikim in the diaspora — where all of this is in the manner of the prayer in the aspect of judgment. For they surrender their body to be buried in the diaspora — where the dominion of the sitra achra resides. And it seems to the sitra achra that it is swallowing this holy body. But this holy body is a great ba'al ko'ach and stands in the sitra achra's throat — until it is compelled through this to vomit greatly from within itself and from its belly — until the Tzadik completes what he began. For even during his lifetime he engaged in this all his days and gave his soul for this. And after his passing, he does not stop engaging in this holy service — until everything is completed for the good as he wishes.

And therefore there — upon his holy grave — every person can be repaired. Even the worst of the worst. If he merits to come there during his lifetime and to request and pray there for the repair of his soul. And this too is the matter of the ten Psalms chapters ordained to be said there — see the inner teachings.

Through meriting to support the Tzadik [financially] — through this it is easier to receive from him the illumination of his holy da'as. Until one can merit through this to eat himself also in great holiness and to receive the illumination of will at the time of eating. Also through this — [through this] — one can receive extra illumination from the remaining da'as [hashoras hada'as] left by the Tzadik — even after his passing.
Also one can receive through this [supporting the Tzadik] an abundant flow of blessing and great wealth.

Through the journey and travel that each person makes from his place to the Tzadik — through this he elevates his place to the aspect of mekomo shel olam [the place of the world] — which is the Tzadik. And this is the aspect of what people journey and travel to the graves of the Tzaddikim — especially before Rosh Hashanah. For in the place where the Tzadik lies — that is the place of his rest — in the aspect of: "they will come to peace; they will rest upon their resting places" [Isaiah 57:2]. And the essential rest of the Tzadik is when he is bound and encompassed in the aspect of the Throne of Glory — the aspect of mekomo shel olam — where the essential rest and the inheritance reside — in the aspect of: "And a glorious throne shall He cause them to inherit, etc." [I Samuel 2:8]. And therefore there — in the place of the Tzadik's resting — every person merits that he will be judged mercifully from Above — and be judged to the scale of merit — through the aspect of mekomo shel olam.

Every time one weeps over the passing of the Tzadik and searches and seeks after him as is proper — then one draws out his holiness through the son or the disciple who fills the place of his father and master. For this is a great principle: the Tzadik does not depart from the world until another is born in his place. As our Sages of blessed memory said [on the verse]: "The sun also rises and the sun also sets, etc." [Ecclesiastes 1:5]. But one must seek and search after this very much — [very much] — especially in these generations.

And therefore even though one must weep and mourn greatly over the passing of the Tzadik — even so, one must be very careful not to stumble through this and say that the Tzadik has already died and there is no more hope, G-d forbid, and that no successor or remnant of him remains in the world. For this is a very great blemish. For certainly the Tzadik has not died — and certainly the remnant [hashoras] of his holiness remains with his sons and his disciples. Only one must search and seek after this very — [very] — greatly. And through every search and seeking, one certainly finds the holiness of his remnant with his sons and disciples. Which is the aspect of: "There Aaron died, and Elazar his son served as priest in his place" [Deuteronomy 10:6] — as explained in the inner teachings.

It is the way of many people to say after the passing of the Tzadik, G-d forbid: "Now we have nothing left at all, G-d forbid." And even though from one side they speak some truth — for certainly there has not remained literally a Tzadik exactly like him. As our Sages of blessed memory said: "The face of Moshe is like the face of the sun; the face of Yehoshua is like the face of the moon. Woe for that shame, etc." — even so, even so, it is forbidden to remain, G-d forbid, with this and to say that therefore all hope is lost, G-d forbid. For the opposite is the case — for G-d will never abandon His people. And "Your dominion is in every generation" [Psalms 145:13]. Therefore one must believe that even though one must certainly pine very greatly after the true Tzadik in the aspect of Moshe — even so, one must conclude with words of comfort — to comfort and gladden oneself in his remnant: that is, the holy innovations of Torah that remain from him through his books and his disciples. For from a truly righteous Tzadik, certainly a good remnant remains forever. Only one must search and seek much as above.

Certainly G-d can sustain the poor and give them all good directly. But the essential commandment of tzedakah is because the money is already in the wealthy person's hand — and it is in his power to do with it as he wishes. And he overpowers [his inclination] through his free will and gives from his own pocket to tzedakah. This is very precious before G-d. For through this he draws chassadim [kindnesses] into the world. And this is His blessed will — that the human being who has free will draw [kindnesses] into the world through the tzedakah he gives to the poor of his own free will. And in all of this we see the greatness of the power of free will.

The repair of all wayfarers — physically and spiritually — is through tzedakah. For the essential knowledge of the truly straight path in its true truth — it is impossible to instruct explicitly, but only through a hint — in the aspect of: "I will instruct you and show you the way you should go — I will counsel you with My eye upon you" [Psalms 32:8]. For it is impossible to explain all the confusions and errors that arise in traveling the paths — even in the physical. How much more so in the matter of spiritual paths and trails in the service of G-d — where it is certainly impossible to explain and specify for each and every person the straight path at every day and every time, as to where to turn to rescue his soul from what needs to be rescued — except through a hint. That a hint is given to a person at every time: "in this way go." And all of this is repaired through tzedakah — in the aspect of: "the righteousness of the wholesome straightens his way" [Proverbs 11:5]. For through tzedakah one merits to walk in the straight path — physically and spiritually.

The virtue of the commandment of tzedakah is without measure — and all the Torah and all the repair of the worlds depends upon this. For everything was created for His honor — and all His honor is revealed through tzedakah. Through which [the world] becomes a vessel to receive the flow of the supernal delight [no'am ha'elyon] — through which birth [holadah] occurs and His honor is revealed. As explained in the inner teachings. And therefore tzedakah is equivalent to the entire Torah — as our Sages of blessed memory said.

But one must give much tzedakah — and request from G-d that he merit to fulfill the commandment of tzedakah as is proper: that he give the tzedakah with a full heart for the sake of His Name, truly. And that G-d send him worthy poor people through whom to merit. For the essential repair of tzedakah is that through it His honor should be magnified as above. And therefore one must intend in his charity only for the honor of G-d — not for his own honor, G-d forbid. Not as is found with many people who give tzedakah only to those who have dominion and prestige in the world — and therefore the tzedakah is also for their honor. And upon the worthy and upright poor who engage in Torah and the service of G-d in truth — they pay no attention to them at all and avert their eyes from them. It is thus found that the tzedakah they give is only for their own honor.

And even though certainly even in such tzedakah there are good points — but through tzedakah such as this, the aforementioned vessel is not made in perfection to receive through it the flow of the supernal delight in perfection. And therefore the essential repair of tzedakah is that it should be in the aspect of a minchah [meal-offering] — which is the sacrifice of the poor person, whose giving is small. And therefore he does not take pride in it — rather, his intention in his offering is only toward Heaven alone. Likewise the wealthy person — even though he gives much to tzedakah — far be it from him to be boastful in the aspect of tzedakah and to intend in it for his own honor. Rather, even though he gives much to tzedakah — even so, in his own eyes he should be like a poor person. For in truth before Him, blessed be He, all are poor — as it is written: "Who can precede Me and I will pay him?" [Job 41:3]. For everything is only from Him, blessed be He. As it is written: "For everything is Yours and from Your hand we have given You" [I Chronicles 29:14]. And therefore King David, peace be upon him, at the time he gave much wealth for the donation toward the Temple said: "And now I have prepared with my poverty, etc." [I Chronicles 29:14] — for he considered all his giving as poverty. And such tzedakah is very precious — for it is the aspect of the minchas ani [offering of the poor] — which is very beloved because his intention is only toward Heaven with no self-glorification whatsoever. And therefore such tzedakah is called by the name minchah — in the aspect of: "those who offer a minchah in righteousness" [Malachi 3:3].

One must give more tzedakah on the Festivals — in order to subdue the forehead [metzach] of the serpent and to reveal the forehead of will [metzach haratzon]. Through which one merits to hear the voice of the herald of Yom Tov — which calls out and reveals the will. Through which one merits the joy of Yom Tov. And this is what our Sages of blessed memory said regarding Yom Tov: "If you gladden Mine — I will gladden yours." For through this one merits the joy of Yom Tov.

Through tzedakah one appeases the burning heat of the heart that blazes toward the desire for sexual union and the desire for money — both of which depend upon one another, as explained in the inner teachings.

Every single person of Israel — in the inner depth of his soul — yearns and burns very greatly for G-d. Because in the inner depth he gazes at all times toward the purpose [tachlis] — which is the light of the Infinite [ohr ha'ain sof] — from which his root derives. And he wishes to cleave and be encompassed there. But since this aspect is in the aspect of ratzo v'shov [advance and retreat] — and when he is in the aspect of shov [retreat], then the vessels of the expanded consciousness [kailim d'hamoi'ach] — which are the aspect of the garments — are unable to receive the light of the shining from there. And then most often the light of the impression [reshimah] of the nullification [bitul] is forgotten from him. And through the commandment of tzitzis — the garments are repaired. Which are the aspect of — [the aspect of] — the vessels of the expanded consciousness. So that they can receive the light of the shining of the impression from the nullification — from which is the root of all Torah. And this is the aspect of: "And you shall see it, etc." [Numbers 15:39] — whose essential [reference] is to the techeiles [blue dye] in the tzitzis. That is, one must look and gaze greatly upon the purpose [tachlis] — which is the aspect of techeiles — as explained in the inner teachings. And this: "and you shall not go astray after your hearts and after your eyes" — that he should close his eyes from the sight of this world entirely and direct his vision and his gaze only toward the purpose alone. "So that you shall remember and do all My commandments" [Numbers 15:40]. For through the commandment of tzitzis one merits to well remember the light of the impression aforementioned — from which flows the totality of Torah and commandments.
Tzitzis is a great protection from the kelipos [husks] and the sitra achra — because within them is bound the light of the aforementioned holy impression.

Tzitzis is the aspect of the repair of the bris — the tikun hakelali [general repair]. For through them the expanded consciousness is elevated and whiteness is drawn to repair the blemishes of all sins, G-d protect us. And through this the garments are repaired and made into the aspect of white garments. And therefore they have thirty-nine [ט"ל] windings — corresponding to the dew of lights [tal orosin] — which one merits through the guarding of the bris. And twelve finger-breadths in length — corresponding to the twelve tribes — in whom his soul is encompassed through the tikun hakelali.
